[maas-code-reviewer review]

> LLM-generated review from https://github.com/canonical/maas-code-reviewer.
> Intended to assist a human reviewer, not replace one — suggestions may be
> incorrect, please verify before acting.


Docs-only change, but two issues go beyond punctuation.

1. Broken link (blocking). `docs/explanation/security.md:110` now points at `https://wiki.ubuntu.com/Full_Disk_Encryption_Howto_2019`, which returns HTTP 404 (verified by fetch). `help.ubuntu.com/community/*` redirects to the new `wiki.ubuntu.com` where legacy community pages were dropped, so the pre-change URL is dead too — the fix is a different target, not a host swap. `docs/.sphinx/.pre-commit-config.yaml` runs `make linkcheck` on `docs/**/*.md`, so this fails locally; CI's `test-docs` job only runs `make lint-md` + `make html`, so it would otherwise ship unnoticed.

2. Stated rationale doesn't match the change or the toolchain. proselint has no check against U+2019; its only quote check is `typography.symbols.curly_quotes`, whose message is literally `Use curly quotes “”, not straight quotes "".` (verified in proselint `checks/typography/symbols.py`), i.e. it pushes the opposite direction and would now flag straight double quotes still present at `manage-machine-groups.md:430`. proselint also appears nowhere in the repo: docs linting is Vale + `pymarkdownlnt` (`docs/Makefile`, `.github/workflows/ci.yaml`). Nothing enforces this convention, so it will drift back.

3. Sweep is partial and leaves mixed typography. Only `’` was converted; `“ ” – —` remain, often in the same sentence (`manage-machine-groups.md:424,437`, `use-cases-server-lifecycle-management.md:19`, `what-maas-shouldn-t-do.md:46`). `deploying-machines.md` only got the URL edit and still has `’` at lines 19, 27, 33, 42, 62, 80.

Suggested shape: (a) fix the FDE link to a live page — `https://documentation.ubuntu.com/security/security-features/storage/encryption-full-disk` resolves and covers LUKS/TPM FDE; (b) decide one source convention (ASCII-only reads best for grep/diff/CLI copy-paste) and apply it to all punctuation across `docs/`, backed by an enforceable rule (Vale rule or pre-commit regex), otherwise this is churn; (c) keep link fixes in a separate commit from the punctuation sweep — unrelated scope in a `docs:` typography PR. Note also that `myst_enable_extensions` in `docs/conf.py:322` does not include `smartquotes`; worth one spot-check of `make html` output that rendered apostrophes still look consistent with neighbouring pages. No security impact.

docs/explanation/security.md.110: Dead link: `https://wiki.ubuntu.com/Full_Disk_Encryption_Howto_2019` returns HTTP 404 (verified). The old `help.ubuntu.com/community/...` URL redirects to this same 404, so both are broken — hard-coding the redirect target doesn't help. Point at a maintained page instead, e.g. `https://documentation.ubuntu.com/security/security-features/storage/encryption-full-disk` (verified live, covers LUKS and TPM-backed FDE). `make linkcheck` (docs pre-commit hook) will fail on the current URL.

docs/explanation/deploying-machines.md.40: `https://canonical.com/juju` resolves fine, but this link swap is unrelated to a punctuation-compliance PR — split it into its own commit so the typography diff stays mechanically reviewable. Also note this file was otherwise untouched: `’` remains at lines 19, 27, 33, 42, 62, 80, so the sweep is inconsistent even within the files it edits.

docs/how-to-guides/manage-machine-groups.424: After this edit the sentence mixes straight apostrophes with curly `“ ”` in the same line, which is worse than either convention consistently applied. proselint's `typography.symbols.curly_quotes` would actually flag the straight double quotes already present at line 430 (`"team A can only deploy machines in pool X."`), so the cited rationale argues the other way. Pick one convention and apply it to apostrophes, double quotes, and dashes together.

docs/uncategorized/what-maas-shouldn-t-d.46: Same mixed-typography result: `don't “just work.”` — straight apostrophe next to curly double quotes. If ASCII punctuation is the target, convert `“ ”` here (lines 46, 50) and the en/em dashes too; otherwise this file ends up with two conventions per sentence.
